lessons.title: Why inline? Lambda Allocation Cost
lessons.content: Every lambda that isn't inlined is compiled to an anonymous class instance - in hot code paths (like a function called inside a RecyclerView scroll listener or a tight loop), this means real allocation overhead. Marking a higher-order function `inline` copies the function body directly to the call site at compile time, eliminating both the lambda object allocation and the function call overhead, and also enables non-local returns from within the lambda.

lessons.title: crossinline and noinline
lessons.content: Inside an inline function, if a lambda parameter is passed further into another context (like a Runnable or a coroutine builder) where a non-local return wouldn't make sense, the compiler requires `crossinline` to explicitly forbid non-local returns from that lambda. `noinline` marks a specific lambda parameter to NOT be inlined - useful when you need to store the lambda as a reference (e.g. pass it to another function) rather than inline its call site.
